svg.title: The First Four Weeks After Close
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-first-30-days-controls; chapter number: 12; title: The First Four Weeks After Close; subtitle: Stabilize cash, people and controls before accelerating; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Employees First, Then Customers; deliverable: Last bank reconciliation for every account, the age of the oldest suspense item, and what the local controller would fix first.; gate: Employees told before customers, and no market blackout.; week: Week 2; title: 13-Week Cash Forecast Live; deliverable: Forecast updated weekly against actuals with every gap explained in writing.; gate: Red flag at a gap above 10% for two consecutive weeks.; week: Week 3; title: Dual Signatures by Day 15; deliverable: Every bank account on dual signatures; the person who approves a payment never sends it.; gate: Lead flow watched; going dark cut it 40% within 3 weeks in the Jen case.; week: Week 4; title: Tribal Knowledge and Access Control; deliverable: Recorded 1 to 2 hour staff sessions converted into SOPs and FAQs; every temporary access given an owner, scope, expiry and removal action.; gate: Day 30 Control Memo in hand before any acceleration.; caption: Operators converge on one rule for the first 100 days: do not break the business, and prove cash visibility and controls in the first month.; assumptions note: Week placement follows the testified deadlines (forecast within 2 weeks, dual signatures by Day 15, Day 30 Control Memo); practitioners split on how fast hard decisions should follow.; note: Attributed to Lighthouse Capital (OwAOc9xgv9U at 00:00:51 and 00:01:07), Neo Expertise (4kQ8R30J5q4 at 00:02:14), Strategy Leaders Inc. (OeJwN9bz5dE at 00:12:31), Patrick O'Connell - M&A Transaction Services (6AT45jrM2CU at 00:23:24) and Bridgeyard (wjVsYwI5G_E at 00:01:58).
